subject: PRD review: Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) — scope + beta/GA milestones

body:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 7, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: PRD review: Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) — scope + beta/GA milestones

Hi all — sharing the PRD for “Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools” and a proposed launch plan. Goal is to get product + eng leadership + security + CS aligned this week so we can lock scope for the first implementation pass.

PRD (v0.8):
- Draft link: (Confluence draft — please use comments mode)
- Attachment: Dedicated_Staged_Rollouts_PRD_v0.8.pdf

Proposed milestones (requesting sign-off / adjustments):
- Week of Jan 13: requirements + UX flows locked (console wizard + stage detail view + approve/abort)
- Feb: control plane + routing integration in staging; dogfood on 1 Redwood-managed dedicated pool
- Beta: 2–3 enterprise Dedicated customers (ops-driven, allowlisted) 
- GA: open to all Dedicated tenants (still ops-driven initially)

Key open questions I’d like your input on:
1) Gate evaluation: do we keep evaluator separate (service/job) vs embed in policy engine? (Priya: I know you’ve got thoughts here.)
2) Audit + approvals: security requirements + retention (Marcus)
3) Dedicated capacity guardrails: minimum headroom / queue depth gating and how we avoid “stage shift -> saturate pool -> violate SLA” (Lauren)
4) Customer comms: how we set expectations for beta + what we can/can’t promise (Rachel)

Paula reviewed the draft gates section and is leaning toward conservative defaults for beta (latency + 5xx + queue depth + missing-metrics hold). I captured her comments in the PRD, but would like Eng/Sec to confirm it’s implementable.

Can you drop comments by EOD Thu (Jan 9) so I can incorporate and circulate a final scope summary on Fri?

Thanks,
Marissa

—
Marissa Cole
Product — Console & Rollouts
Redwood Inference



From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 7, 2025 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: PRD review: Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) — scope + beta/GA milestones

Thanks Marissa.

Dedicated-specific feedback (biggest risks):
- Any stage shift changes effective capacity for the “new” version in a fixed-size reserved pool. If the new version is slower (or worse at batching) we’ll induce queue depth and blow latency before a gate even triggers.
- For Dedicated we need an explicit “minimum headroom” constraint. I’d prefer a hard block on advancing if (a) GPU util is already high or (b) queue depth is above baseline.

Concrete recs for beta:
- Keep stage sizes conservative: 5% -> 25% -> 100% (skip 50/75). We can always add more stage presets later.
- Default gating should include queue depth and timeouts, not just p95/p99 latency. Queue depth is the earlier signal in reserved pools.
- I want SRE sign-off as a requirement before enablement for any customer tenant (even in beta). This is too easy to accidentally turn into a customer-visible incident.

I’ll add a few PRD comments re: guardrails + the “what happens if pool constrained” section.

Lauren

—
Lauren Bishop
Product — Dedicated
Redwood Inference



From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 7, 2025 at 11:27 AM PT
Subject: Re: PRD review: Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) — scope + beta/GA milestones

Reviewed. High-level + a few engineering constraints to bake into the PRD so we don’t scope ourselves into a corner.

Gate evaluation placement:
- Strong preference: evaluator as a separate server-side component that writes “gate results” + “advance/hold recommendation” into the rollout state.
- Policy engine should only consume a stable “stage weight” / “stage state” output. Embedding evaluation logic into policy would make policy evaluation stateful + harder to reason about / test.

State machine + idempotency:
- Approvals must be idempotent and resilient to retries; assume concurrent approval requests and evaluator ticks.
- Plan needs optimistic concurrency (plan_version) and an append-only event log for audit + debugging.

Missing/late metrics behavior:
- For Dedicated: fail safe = hold. Do not advance stages if freshness is unknown.
- Make “metrics freshness” itself a first-class evaluation input so we can alert on evaluator / telemetry lag separately.

Timeline feasibility:
- If we want dogfood in Feb, we need the control-plane objects (Plan/Stage/Gate/ApprovalEvent) defined + codegen’d early.
- I’d propose: lock schemas + API contracts by Jan 17, so Platform can start implementation without churn.

I’ll leave PRD comments (esp. on “non-goals”: quality gating should be explicitly out of v1 unless we have a pre-existing signal pipeline).

Priya

—
Priya Natarajan
Engineering (Platform Architecture)
Redwood Inference



From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 7, 2025 at 1:06 PM PT
Subject: Re: PRD review: Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) — scope + beta/GA milestones

Adding security/compliance requirements to incorporate:

Audit logging (must-have for Dedicated):
- Emit structured audit events for: rollout_plan.create, rollout_plan.update, rollout.approve_stage, rollout.abort, rollout.auto_hold, rollout.auto_rollback.
- Each event needs: actor (user/service), actor_type, tenant_id, pool_id, rollout_plan_id, plan_version, stage_id, previous_state -> new_state, and a “reason” field (e.g., gate failure: p95_latency, missing_metrics, queue_depth).

Retention:
- Default retention aligned with existing audit pipeline; for Dedicated enterprise we should plan for 12 months minimum (customers frequently ask for “who approved what change when”).

RBAC:
- Separate permissions for edit vs approve vs abort. Approve should be limited to a smaller set of operator roles.
- PRD should clarify whether customers ever self-approve in v1 (I’d recommend no; at most enterprise opt-in with explicit roles).

Data minimization:
- Do not include prompt/content data in audit events. Avoid high-cardinality fields.

I’ll comment in PRD with the event schema requirements and a note on SOC2-style change management language.

Marcus

—
Marcus Lin
Security
Redwood Inference



From: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 8, 2025 at 8:41 AM PT
Subject: Re: PRD review: Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) — scope + beta/GA milestones

From the CS side:

- We have active pain on this (SUP-3917: rollout-induced latency spikes, SUP-3981: audit trail requested for compliance).
- Two accounts have already asked for “staged” / “canary” semantics specifically for reserved pools, not just “update the pool.”

Beta expectations:
- We should message beta as operator-driven + allowlist only. Customers are fine with that as long as the behavior is clear and we can show audit entries.
- Success criteria for beta should include: (1) customer can see stage status + hold reason, (2) we can quickly abort/rollback, and (3) we can prove approvals/audit in a security review.

Customer comms:
- Please avoid promising “A/B testing” in the staged rollouts messaging. They conflate this with experimentation; what they want is “safer updates.”

If helpful I can share the exact customer language from SUP-3981 in a comment.

Rachel

—
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Customer Success
Redwood Inference



From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 9, 2025 at 4:22 PM PT
Subject: Re: PRD review: Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) — scope + beta/GA milestones

Thanks all. A few decisions + constraints so we can move quickly but safely.

Decisions (approved direction):
1) Evaluator lives server-side (separate component) and policy/routing consumes stage weights + stage state only. (Agree with Priya.)
2) Fail-safe: if metrics are missing/late, we HOLD (no automatic advancement). No exceptions for Dedicated.
3) Dedicated enablement requires SRE sign-off prior to any customer beta.

Launch expectations:
- Beta should include strong operator tooling: approve/abort + visibility into “why held” + audit log export compatibility.

Milestones (updated proposal):
- Jan 17: PRD + schemas + API contract locked.
- Feb 10: end-to-end in staging (create -> stage 1 -> hold on gate failure -> abort).
- Week of Mar 3: beta start (2 customers max, allowlisted).
- Week of Apr 7: target GA, contingent on SRE readiness + audit completeness.

Please incorporate into the PRD and share a 1-page “scope lock + dependencies” recap. I’m fine with the scope as long as quality gating is explicitly not a v1 dependency.

Neha

—
Neha Kapoor
Product & Engineering Leadership
Redwood Inference



From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 10, 2025 at 9:18 AM PT
Subject: Re: PRD review: Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) — scope + beta/GA milestones

Aligned — thank you.

I updated the PRD to reflect the decisions and added a “scope lock” section (including the explicit non-goal of per-request semantic quality gating in v1).

Summary of decisions (as captured):
- Gate evaluator: separate server-side evaluator writes gate results + stage state; routing reads stage weights/state.
- Fail safe: missing/late metrics => HOLD (no auto advance).
- Dedicated enablement: requires SRE sign-off pre-beta.

Default stage preset for beta:
- Stage 1: 5%
- Stage 2: 25%
- Stage 3: 100%

Default gates for beta (configurable; conservative defaults):
- p95 latency threshold (route/model scoped)
- 5xx / timeout rate threshold
- queue depth threshold (Dedicated-specific)
- “metrics freshness” gate (explicit; failing triggers HOLD)

Approvals + audit logging:
- Separate permissions: edit vs approve vs abort.
- Audit events include auto_hold and auto_rollback.

Milestones (per Neha):
- Jan 17: PRD + schemas/API locked
- Feb 10: E2E in staging
- Week of Mar 3: beta start (max 2 customers; allowlist)
- Week of Apr 7: GA target (subject to SRE + security sign-off)

Paula’s notes (she’s not on this thread): she agrees we should default to HOLD rather than auto-rollback in beta unless the gate is “hard fail” (e.g., error rate). I captured this as: HOLD by default, rollback as an optional policy.

Attachment: Dedicated_Staged_Rollouts_PRD_v0.9_changes_summary.txt

Next step: if no objections by Tue (Jan 14), I’ll treat this as scope lock and convert the milestones into the initiative plan.

Marissa

—
Marissa Cole
